prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1237; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot and stated they were struck while stopped in a marked space. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Neck and back strain reported; initial recorded account is consistent with the vehicle damage and the force involved.

Entry 2: Police report, two independent witnesses, and the other driver all confirm the accident occurred as described and that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Photos taken at the scene are on file.

Entry 3: Claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far, with no changes to the sequence of events. Claimant's prior medical history notes a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed completely without lasting effects.

Entry 4: Treatment has followed a typical course for this type of injury, with symptoms easing steadily as the claimant improved. Care has been tapering off in line with recovery. Reviewed the timeline of treatment against the reported injury and found it reasonable.

Entry 5: A dated inspection photo from before this collision shows the same dent on the vehicle, so part of the damage predates this loss. It is not yet clear whether all of the damage in the current estimate came from this impact. Referred to the appraiser for a line-by-line review.

Entry 6: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date. The driver is named on the policy. Claim remains open pending the appraiser's apportionment of the prior damage and final medical review.
